p.src: After Daiyu resolved to take her own life, her strength gradually failed, until one day she stopped eating altogether. For more than ten days Grandmother Jia and the others had taken turns visiting her, and at first she would still say a few words now and then, but for the past two days she had scarcely spoken at all. Though her mind sometimes drifted into a stupor, at other times it was perfectly clear. Grandmother Jia and the others could see that her illness had not arisen without cause, and twice questioned Zijuan and Xueyan closely, but neither girl dared say anything. Even Zijuan, who wanted to ask Shishu what news she had heard, feared that further commotion might make the rumor seem true and hasten Daiyu's death; so whenever she saw Shishu, she said nothing about it. As for Xueyan, it was her relaying of the tale that had brought matters to this pass. She now wished she had a hundred mouths with which to protest, “I never said it,” and naturally dared even less to mention the subject. On the day Daiyu ceased eating entirely, Zijuan gave up all hope. After sitting beside her and weeping for a while, she slipped outside and whispered to Xueyan, “Go in and keep a close watch over her. I am going to inform the Old Lady, the Mistress, and Second Mistress. Her condition today is nothing like it has been before.” Xueyan assented, and Zijuan went off alone.

p.src: Xueyan stayed in the room with Daiyu and watched her sink into a heavy stupor. Young as she was, she had never seen such a sight and supposed this must be what dying looked like. Heartsick and terrified, she longed for Zijuan to return at once. Just as her fear mounted, she heard footsteps outside the window. Thinking Zijuan had returned, she felt relieved, hurriedly rose, and held up the inner curtain to await her. But when the outer curtain rustled and someone entered, it proved to be Shishu. Tanchun had sent Shishu to inquire after Daiyu. Seeing Xueyan holding up the curtain, she asked, “How is Miss Daiyu?” Xueyan nodded and beckoned her inside. Shishu followed her in. Finding Zijuan absent, she looked at Daiyu and saw that only the faintest thread of breath remained. Shocked and alarmed, she asked, “Where is Sister Zijuan?” “She has gone to tell those in the main house,” replied Xueyan. By now Xueyan assumed that Daiyu was entirely insensible, and with Zijuan away, she quietly took Shishu by the hand and asked, “Was it true, what you told me the other day—that Master Wang had proposed a match for Second Master Bao?” “Of course it was true,” said Shishu. “When were the betrothal gifts exchanged?” asked Xueyan. “It has not gone so far as a betrothal yet,” said Shishu. When I told you about it that day, I was only repeating what I had heard Xiaohong say. Later I went to Second Mistress's quarters and heard her talking with Sister Ping. She said the retainers were only using this affair to curry favor with Master Jia, hoping to gain his support later. The First Mistress herself disapproved; and even if she had favored the match and praised the girl, what sort of person could the First Mistress ever judge correctly? Besides, the Old Lady has long had someone in mind, and she is right here in our garden. How could the First Mistress know what the Old Lady intends? The Old Lady merely made inquiries because Master Jia had spoken of it and she could hardly refuse. I also heard Second Mistress say that, in Baoyu's marriage, the Old Lady means to strengthen ties already within the family. No matter who comes to propose another match, it will never succeed.” Hearing this, Xueyan forgot herself and exclaimed, “What does this mean? We have sacrificed our young lady's life for nothing!” “Whatever do you mean by that?” asked Shishu. “You still do not know,” said Xueyan. The other day Sister Zijuan and I were talking about that very thing. Our young lady overheard us, and that is what has brought her to this state.” “Speak more softly,” said Shishu. “Take care that she does not hear you.” “She is no longer conscious of anything,” said Xueyan. “Just look at her. She has no more than a day or two left.”

p.src: As they were speaking, Zijuan lifted the curtain and came in, crying, “This is intolerable! Whatever you have to say, why do you not go outside and say it instead of talking here? You may as well hound her to death and be done with it.” “I cannot believe anything so extraordinary could happen,” said Shishu. “My dear sister,” said Zijuan, “do not take offense at what I am about to say. What do you understand about it? If you understood, you would never have spread such gossip.”

p.src: While the three of them were talking, they suddenly heard Daiyu cough again. Zijuan hurried to the edge of the kang and stood there, while Shishu and Xueyan both fell silent. Bending over behind Daiyu, Zijuan asked softly, “Miss, would you like a sip of water?” Daiyu murmured her assent. Xueyan promptly poured half a cup of freshly boiled water. Zijuan took it and held it, while Shishu also stepped closer. Zijuan shook her head at Shishu to stop her from speaking, so Shishu had no choice but to swallow her words. After they had stood there a while, Daiyu coughed once more. Seizing the opportunity, Zijuan asked, “Would you like some water, Miss?” Daiyu again gave a faint reply. She seemed to want to raise her head, but could not lift it. Zijuan climbed onto the kang and knelt beside Daiyu. Holding the water, she tested its temperature, brought the bowl to Daiyu’s lips, and supported her head until it reached the rim, whereupon Daiyu took a sip. Just as Zijuan was about to take the bowl away, Daiyu appeared to want another sip, so Zijuan held it where it was. Daiyu drank once more, then shook her head to show she wanted no more. After catching her breath, she lay down again. After a long while, she opened her eyes slightly and said, “Wasn’t that Shishu speaking just now?” “Yes,” Zijuan replied. Shishu had not yet left, so she hastened over to inquire after Daiyu. Daiyu opened her eyes and looked at her, nodded, and after resting a little longer said, “Go back and give my regards to your young mistress.” Seeing her in this state, Shishu supposed that Daiyu found her presence bothersome and had no choice but to withdraw quietly. In fact, although Daiyu was gravely ill, her mind was still lucid. When Shishu and Xueyan first began talking, she had dimly caught part of what they said, but pretended not to know, for she truly lacked the strength to respond. But after hearing the rest of Xueyan and Shishu’s conversation, she realized that the earlier proposal had only been discussed and never settled. Moreover, Shishu had said that Xifeng had spoken of the Old Lady’s plan to unite two branches of the family in marriage, and that the chosen girl lived in the Garden. Who could it be but herself? At this thought, as yang is born when yin reaches its extreme, her mind and spirits suddenly felt much refreshed. That was why she drank two sips of water and wanted to question Shishu. Just then, Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, Li Wan, and Xifeng, having heard what Zijuan had said, all hurried in to see Daiyu. The knot of doubt in Daiyu’s heart had now been untied, so naturally she no longer wished for death as she had before. Though physically weak and short of energy, she could now force herself to answer a word or two. Xifeng called Zijuan over and asked, “Surely your young mistress wasn’t in such a desperate state. What do you mean by giving us such a fright?” “She truly looked very bad earlier, or I would never have dared report it,” Zijuan replied. “But when I came back, I found her much better. It is strange indeed.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Don’t blame her. What does she understand?

p.src: Leaving aside how Daiyu’s illness gradually abated, we turn to Xueyan and Zijuan, who both privately gave thanks to Buddha. Xueyan said to Zijuan, “Thank goodness she recovered! It was a strange illness, and her recovery was just as strange.” “There was nothing strange about her falling ill,” said Zijuan. “The only strange thing was her recovery. It seems to me that Baoyu and our young mistress must be destined for marriage. People say, ‘Good things meet with many trials,’ and also, ‘A predestined match cannot be broken even with a cudgel.’ Judging by all this, both human feeling and Heaven’s will show that the two of them are truly a match made in heaven. Besides, remember how, that year, I said Miss Lin was going back south? Baoyu nearly died of anxiety, and the whole household was thrown into turmoil. Now a single remark has brought this one to the brink of death and back again. Doesn’t that prove their bond was forged a hundred years ago upon the Stone of Three Lives?” At this, the two of them quietly pursed their lips and smiled together for a while. Xueyan added, “Thank goodness she recovered. From now on, we must never say such things again. Even if Baoyu marries some other family’s daughter, and I see the wedding with my own eyes, I shall never breathe a word of it.” Zijuan laughed. “That is just as it should be.” It was not only Zijuan and Xueyan who discussed the matter in private. Everyone knew that Daiyu had fallen ill in a strange way and recovered in a way just as strange, and they gathered in twos and threes to whisper about it. Before long, even Xifeng heard of it. Ladies Xing and Wang were also somewhat puzzled, while Grandmother Jia had already guessed nearly the whole truth.

p.src: Just then, Ladies Xing and Wang, Xifeng, and the others were chatting in Grandmother Jia's room, and the conversation turned to Daiyu's illness. Grandmother Jia said, “I have been meaning to speak to you about this. Baoyu and that girl Lin have been together since childhood, and I always thought, ‘They are only children—what is there to fear?’ But lately I have often heard that she suddenly falls ill and then suddenly recovers, all because she has begun to understand such matters. So I think that if we keep letting them stay together, it will ultimately be improper. What do you think?” Lady Wang was taken aback when she heard this, but could only reply, “Miss Lin is a thoughtful and perceptive girl. As for Baoyu, he may be foolish and heedless of appearances, but outwardly he still seems entirely like a child. If we suddenly moved either one of them out of the Garden now, would that not make it obvious that something was amiss? As the old saying goes, ‘A grown man must wed, and a grown woman must marry.’ Perhaps, if you think fit, madam, it would be best to hasten their marriages.” Grandmother Jia frowned and said, “That girl Lin's peculiar temperament is in one sense a virtue, yet it is precisely why I do not intend to match her with Baoyu. Besides, she is so frail that I fear she may not be long-lived. Only that girl Bao is truly suitable.” Lady Wang said, “You are not alone in thinking so, madam; we think the same. But we ought to find Miss Lin a husband too. Otherwise, what grown girl is without thoughts of her own? If she truly harbors private feelings for Baoyu and then learns that he is betrothed to that girl Bao, something dreadful may happen.” Grandmother Jia said, “Naturally we must first see Baoyu married, and only afterward arrange a match for that girl Lin. We cannot possibly put an outsider before one of our own. Besides, that girl Lin is, after all, two years younger than Baoyu. From what you say, then, it would be best not to let her know of Baoyu's betrothal.” Xifeng then ordered all the maids, “You heard what was said. You are not to go about babbling that Second Master Bao is to be betrothed. Anyone who talks too much had better look to her hide.” Grandmother Jia then said to Xifeng, “Feng, since your health began to fail, you have not been attending much to affairs in the Garden. Let me tell you, you must pay more attention. It is not only this matter; those people drinking and gambling the year before last were intolerable too. You are the most capable one, so you will have to spare more attention and keep a tighter rein on them. Besides, as I see it, you are the only one they still obey.” Xifeng assented. The ladies talked for a while longer before going their separate ways. From then on, Xifeng often went to the Garden to oversee matters.

p.src: One day, just after entering Prospect Garden and reaching the shore of Water Caltrop Isle, she heard an old woman shouting there. When Xifeng approached, the woman finally noticed her. She at once stood respectfully with her hands lowered and offered a greeting. Xifeng asked, “What are you making such a commotion about?” The woman replied, “The mistresses assigned me to guard the flowers and fruit here, and I have done nothing wrong. Yet, to my surprise, Miss Xing's maid called us thieves.” “Why?” asked Xifeng. The woman said, “Yesterday my Hei'er followed me here and played for a while. Not knowing any better, he went over to take a look around Miss Xing's quarters, but I sent him home. Early this morning, I heard their maids say something had gone missing. When I asked what they had lost, the maid began questioning me instead.” Xifeng said, “There was no need to get angry merely because she asked you a question.” The woman said, “After all, this Garden belongs to your family, madam, not to theirs. We were all appointed by you, madam. How could we accept being branded thieves?” Xifeng spat in her face and snapped, “Stop prattling in front of me! You are responsible for watching this place. If a young lady loses something, of course you should be questioned. How dare you utter such unreasonable words? Send for Old Lin and have her driven out.” The maids acknowledged the order. Just then Xing Xiuyan hurried out and greeted Xifeng with an apologetic smile. “You must not do that. Nothing happened, and the matter is already over.” Xifeng said, “Miss, that is not the point. Quite apart from the incident itself, her disregard for proper rank is utterly outrageous.” Seeing the woman kneeling on the ground and pleading for mercy, Xiuyan hastened to invite Xifeng inside to sit down. Xifeng said, “I know people like her. Except when I am present, they show no respect to anyone above or below them.” Xiuyan pleaded for the woman again and again, insisting that her own maid had been at fault. Xifeng said, “For Miss Xing's sake, I shall spare you this once.” Only then did the woman rise. She kowtowed to Xifeng, then to Xiuyan, and finally withdrew.

p.src: The two women then courteously invited each other to sit. Xifeng asked with a smile, “What did you lose?” Xiuyan smiled. “Nothing important—only a little red padded jacket, and an old one at that. I merely told them to look for it and said that if they could not find it, they should let the matter drop. This young maid did not know any better and questioned that woman, who naturally took offense. It was all because the little maid was foolish and ignorant. I have already scolded her, and the matter is over, so there is no need to mention it again.” Xifeng looked Xiuyan over from head to foot. Though she wore some fur-lined, padded garments, they were already neither new nor quite old and could hardly have kept her warm. Her bedding was probably thin as well. As for the objects displayed on the table in her room, although the Old Lady had given them to her, she had not touched a single one, but kept them all spotlessly clean. Xifeng felt great affection and respect for her and said, “One garment may not ordinarily matter, but the weather is cold, and it was worn next to the body. Why should you not ask about it? That insolent servant has become altogether intolerable!” After talking for a while, Xifeng left, called briefly at various places, and then returned home. Once in her own room, she told Ping'er to fetch a little jacket of bright-red foreign crepe, a small fur jacket of pine-pollen-colored damask patterned with strings of pearls, a padded skirt of sapphire-blue brocade with an embroidered border, and a dark-blue jacket lined with silver-squirrel fur. She had them wrapped up and sent to Xiuyan.

Xifeng asked with a smile, “What did you lose?”

I merely told them to look for it and said that if they could not find it, they should let the matter drop.
This young maid did not know any better and questioned that woman, who naturally took offense.
It was all because the little maid was foolish and ignorant. I have already scolded her, and the matter is over, so there is no need to mention it again.”
Xifeng looked Xiuyan over from head to foot. Though she wore some fur-lined, padded garments, they were already neither new nor quite old and could hardly have kept her warm.
Her bedding was probably thin as well.
As for the objects displayed on the table in her room, although the Old Lady had given them to her, she had not touched a single one, but kept them all spotlessly clean.
Xifeng felt great affection and respect for her and said, “One garment may not ordinarily matter, but the weather is cold, and it was worn next to the body. Why should you not ask about it?
That insolent servant has become altogether intolerable!”
After talking for a while, Xifeng left, called briefly at various places, and then returned home.

Once in her own room, she told Ping'er to fetch a little jacket of bright-red foreign crepe, a small fur jacket of pine-pollen-colored damask patterned with strings of pearls, a padded skirt of sapphire-blue brocade with an embroidered border, and a dark-blue jacket lined with silver-squirrel fur. She had them wrapped up and sent to Xiuyan.

p.src: By then, Xiuyan had endured a bout of scolding from the old woman. Although Xifeng had come and silenced her, Xiuyan still felt uneasy. She thought, “With so many of the young ladies living here, not one servant dares offend any of them. Only with me do they make one insinuation after another—and just now Xifeng happened to witness it.” The more she turned it over in her mind, the more wretched she felt, yet she could tell no one. As she was stifling her sobs and weeping in silence, she saw Feng'er coming from Xifeng's quarters with some clothes. The moment Xiuyan saw them, she firmly refused to accept them. Feng'er said, “Mistress told me to say that if you dislike them because they are old clothes, she will send you new ones instead.” Xiuyan smiled and thanked her. “I am deeply grateful for your mistress's kindness, but she sent these only because I lost my coat, and I would never dare accept them. Please take them back and convey my deepest thanks to your mistress. I shall count her kindness as fully received.” Instead, she gave Feng'er a purse. Feng'er had no choice but to take it and leave. Before long, Ping'er appeared with Feng'er. Xiuyan hurried forward to greet them and invited them to sit down. Ping'er said with a smile, “Our mistress says you are being altogether far too formal with her.” “It is not that I mean to be formal,” said Xiuyan. “I simply feel that I cannot accept them in good conscience.” Ping'er replied, “Mistress says that if you refuse the clothes, you must either think them too old or look down upon her. She told me just now that if I brought them back, she would not forgive me.” Blushing, Xiuyan smiled and thanked her. “When you put it that way, I dare not refuse them.” She then pressed tea upon them once more.

p.src: As Ping'er and Feng'er were returning and had nearly reached Xifeng's quarters, they met an old woman sent by the Xue household, who came up and greeted them. Ping'er asked, “Where have you come from?” The old woman replied, “The mistress and young lady over there sent me to inquire after all the ladies, mistresses, and young ladies here. Just now, when I asked our mistress about you, she said you had gone into the garden. Have you come from Miss Xing's place?” “How did you know?” asked Ping'er. “I heard about it just now,” replied the old woman. Truly, Second Mistress and you young ladies act with a kindness that moves the heart.” Ping'er smiled and said, “Come and sit with us when you return.” “I still have errands to attend to,” said the old woman. “I shall come and see you another day.” With that, she went away. Ping'er returned and reported everything to Xifeng. But no more need be said of that.

p.src: Meanwhile, Aunt Xue's household had been thrown into utter turmoil by Jingui. When the old woman returned and related what had happened to Xiuyan, Baochai and her mother could not help shedding tears. Baochai said, “It is all because Elder Brother is away from home that Miss Xing must endure several more days of hardship. Fortunately, Cousin Xifeng has treated her well. We must also take greater care of her from now on; after all, she belongs to our family.” As she spoke, Xue Ke came in and said, “What sort of people has Elder Brother been associating with outside these past few years? There is not one respectable man among them. Whenever a pack of them turns up, they are nothing but a gang of scoundrels. I can see they have not come out of concern for him; they merely mean to sound us out for news. I have driven every one of them away these past two days. I shall instruct the gatekeepers not to admit such people again.” Aunt Xue asked, “Was it Jiang Yuhan and his sort again?” “Jiang Yuhan did not come,” replied Xue Ke. “They were others.” Hearing Xue Ke's words, Aunt Xue was overcome with grief once more. “I have a son,” she said, “yet now it is as though I had none. Even if the authorities approve his release, he will be a ruined man. Though you are my nephew, I find you more sensible than your cousin. For the rest of my life, I shall depend entirely upon you. From now on, you yourself must strive all the harder to be good. Besides, the family circumstances of the young woman to whom you are betrothed are not what they once were. It is no small matter for another family's daughter to marry. She has no other hopes, but trusts that if her husband is capable, she will have a decent life. If that Xing girl were like this creature—” Here she pointed toward the inner rooms. “Then I would have nothing more to say. But the Xing girl truly has a sense of honor and good judgment; she can remain steadfast in poverty and conduct herself properly in wealth. Once our present troubles are past, you should settle your proper affair as soon as possible. That would lift one burden from my heart.” Xue Ke said, “Cousin Qin has not yet married; that is one matter over which you truly need to concern yourself. As for my affair, what is there to worry about?” They continued chatting idly for a while.

p.src: Xue Ke returned to his room and ate his evening meal. He thought of Xing Xiuyan living in the garden of the Jia residence, dependent upon another household and poor besides; what her daily life must be like scarcely needed imagining. Moreover, they had traveled here together in the beginning, so he knew both her appearance and her character. Plainly Heaven dealt unequally with people: someone like Xia Jingui was perversely granted wealth and reared in such indulgence that she became utterly overbearing, while someone like Xing Xiuyan was perversely made to suffer so. He wondered by what principles the King of Hell allotted men's destinies. Growing oppressed by these thoughts, he wished to compose a poem and set it down to vent the gloom in his breast. But he lamented his own lack of skill, and could only scribble these rough lines:

p.src: A dragon bereft of water is like a stranded fish; in two distant places, lonely hearts lament their solitude.

u.src: A dragon bereft of water is like a stranded fish; in two distant places, lonely hearts lament their solitude.

p.src: Together mired in mud, we suffer bitterly; when shall we rise into the pure, empty sky?

p.src: When he had finished writing, he looked it over for a while and thought of pasting it on the wall, but felt too embarrassed. He mused to himself, “I must not let anyone see it and laugh at me.” He read it through once more and said, “Oh, what does it matter? I may as well paste it up and look at it myself to relieve the tedium.” After looking it over yet again, however, he still thought it improper and put it between the leaves of a book. Then he reflected that he himself was no longer so young, while his family had been struck by such unforeseen calamity, with no knowing when it would end, leaving a frail maiden secluded in her chamber in such misery and loneliness. While he was absorbed in these thoughts, Baochan pushed open the door and came in carrying a box, which she set on the table with a beaming smile. Xue Ke rose and invited her to sit down. Smiling, Baochan said to Xue Ke, “Here are four dishes of fruit and a small flask of wine. The young mistress told me to bring them to you, Second Master.” Xue Ke answered with a courteous smile, “It was very thoughtful of the young mistress. But she need only have sent one of the little maids. Why trouble you to come yourself?” “Please, think nothing of it,” said Baochan. We are all one family, Second Master. Why stand on such ceremony? Besides, the affair concerning our master has truly caused you a great deal of trouble. The young mistress has long wished to prepare something herself to thank you, but she was afraid that others might misconstrue it. You know yourself, Second Master, that in this household people agree in words but not in their hearts. There is nothing improper about sending a few things, yet it would only provoke all manner of gossip and criticism. So today she prepared just a little fruit and a flask of wine and told me to bring them to you quietly in person.” As she spoke, she cast Xue Ke another smiling glance and said, “In future, Second Master, please do not say such things again. It is terribly embarrassing if anyone hears you. We are merely servants. If we may wait upon the elder master, we may also wait upon the second. What harm could there be in that?” Xue Ke was honest and good-natured by disposition and, after all, still young. Although neither Jingui nor Baochan had ever treated him in this way before, he reflected that Baochan’s explanation about Xue Pan was reasonable enough, and so he said, “Leave the fruit, then, but please take the wine back with you. I have never had much capacity for wine. When pressed, I may occasionally drink a single cup, but I cannot drink on ordinary days when there is no occasion. Surely the young mistress and you both know that?” Baochan replied, “I can decide about anything else, but this one matter I dare not agree to. You know the young mistress’s temper, Second Master. If I take it back, instead of saying that you would not drink it, she will accuse me of failing to do my duty.” Xue Ke had no choice but to keep it. Baochan was just about to leave when she went to the doorway and looked outside. Turning back, she smiled at Xue Ke, pointed toward the inner rooms, and said, “I should not be surprised if she comes herself to thank you for your trouble.”

p.src: Not understanding what she meant, Xue Ke grew awkward instead and said, “Please thank the young mistress on my behalf. The weather is cold; she must take care not to catch a chill. Besides, we are sister-in-law and younger brother within the same family, so there is no need for such formalities.” Baochan made no reply and left with a smile.

Besides, we are sister-in-law and younger brother within the same family, so there is no need for such formalities.”
Baochan made no reply and left with a smile.

p.src: At first, Xue Ke supposed that Jingui might truly have felt guilty about the trouble caused by Xue Pan’s affair and had prepared the wine and fruit to thank him for his efforts; that was quite possible. But after seeing Baochan behave in such a furtive and equivocal manner, he began to perceive something of the truth. Then he reconsidered: “She is, after all, my sister-in-law. How could there possibly be some other intention behind it? Perhaps Baochan is merely immature and, too embarrassed to make advances on her own account, has used Jingui’s name as a pretext. That too is possible. Yet she belongs to my brother’s household, so that would be improper too.” Suddenly another thought occurred to him: “Jingui has never had the least regard for the proprieties expected of a gentlewoman. Moreover, when the fancy takes her, she dresses herself in an exceedingly provocative fashion and thinks herself beautiful. Who can say that she is not harboring some wicked design? Or else perhaps she has had some falling-out with Cousin Qin and has devised this vicious scheme to drag me into muddy waters and stain my reputation with an ambiguous scandal.” At this thought, he became thoroughly frightened. While he was still at a loss what to do, he suddenly heard a stifled laugh outside the window, which made him jump in alarm. Who it was will be revealed in the next chapter.
